earlier_scan.source_named: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area. De Gruyter Mouton — contains Kimki sketch data; volume paywalled

sources.citation: OLAC resources in and about the Kimki language (sbt), Internet Archive copy 2025-01-23; Glottolog 5.3 languoid page kimk1238.
sources.note: Catalog checks only: no grammar, sketch or phonology is registered for Kimki anywhere (Glottolog descriptive refs = 0; OLAC = Glottolog + Ethnologue entries only).

sources.citation: Arnold, Laura. 2025. Language as a lens into the prehistory of West New Guinea. In: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories (Terra Australis 58), chapter 3, 18 pp. Canberra: ANU Press. doi:10.22459/TA58.2024.03
sources.note: map/list of families and isolates only; the chapter's only prosody content concerns contact-induced tone in SHWNG Austronesian languages of Raja Ampat/Cenderawasih Bay, not the isolates

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [last modified 2024-06-25]. South Pauwasi River. Newguineaworld (UZH DokuWiki).
sources.note: Historical phonology of Proto-South Pauwasi with Kimki (Batom, Sabi) reflexes from Rumaropen (2004). No statement about stress; a handful of Kimki forms are cited with IPA stress marks (naˈme '1pl', pu-ˈme '2sg', it-ˈba 'skin', -ˈlikʰ 'knee', na-me-ˈpaːr '1pl.incl', ˈsiburɔ 'sweet potato'), i.e. the survey wordlist marks stress phonetically but no rule is given.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. Kimki. Newguineaworld (UZH DokuWiki page; also old Google Sites page, Internet Archive copy 2022-10-06).
sources.note: Nothing: both the current UZH page and the archived Google Sites page are empty stubs (title only).

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. n.d. [c. 2017-2019]. Bahasa Kimki (Provinsi Papua). Peta Bahasa, entry idb=481; same text printed in Bahasa dan Peta Bahasa di Indonesia (Jakarta: Badan Bahasa, 2018 printing), p. 213, sec. 2.8.1.120.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content: location, neighbouring languages as reported by residents, and dialectometry ('isolek Kimki merupakan sebuah bahasa dengan persentase perbedaan berkisar 98,50%-100% jika dibandingkan dengan.. Mukim [Murkim], Namalu, dan Warion'). Implies an unpublished Badan Bahasa/Balai Bahasa Papua Swadesh-type wordlist from Batom exists.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2012. Pronouns and the (preliminary) classification of Papuan languages. In Harald Hammarström & Wilco van den Heuvel (eds.), History, contact and classification of Papuan languages (Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2012, Part 2), 428-539. Port Moresby: Linguistic Society of Papua New Guinea.
sources.note: No phonology content for Kimki. The article is a statistical study of pronoun-form similarity across Papuan families; Kimki appears (i) in footnote 9, p. c. 447: 'Kimki is an extremely poorly known language from the remote area between the upper Sepik and Sobger rivers. The source for the ASJP list (Whitehouse 1980) has 1P SG win and 2P SG omE ~ umE, but the only other source on Kimki (Rumaropen 2004) has a different 2P SG form pume (Kimki of Batom) ~ Fume (Kimki of Sabi) with an initial labial stop or fricative', with a remark that a Ndu-Kimki link 'remains to be investigated'; (ii) in the a…

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212. hdl:10125/4478
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.4.10 (pp. 188-189): the only substantial Kimki data are an unpublished 250-word list and fifteen sentences in an SIL survey report (Rumaropen 2004), plus an 11-word list from Langeler 1915.

sources.citation: Whitehouse, Paul. 2006. The "Lost" Paper: A Belated Conference Postscript. Mother Tongue: Journal of the Association for the Study of Language in Prehistory XI: 262-274.
sources.note: Nothing: a long-range classification essay (Kehu, Bulaka River-Trans Fly, expanded Pauwasi); Kimgi appears once in the grouping proposal and twice as a lexical comparandum; no transcription carries stress marks and the words stress/tone/accent do not occur in the article.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: ANU. 476 pp. (language index entries e.g. 'Sause (SW of Sentani) Barrs 1978, Kana 1975, Voorhoeve 1975, W&H 1981'; 'Tanahmerah 1 (N Bomberai Pen'a; also Sumeri, Sumerine) Barrs, Voorhoeve 1975..'; 'Yetfa (border IJ) SH'; author entries REIMER & SONGKILAWANG 1980 Suku-Batong survey report MS; KANA, Marit 1975 Languages of Kabupaten Jayapura MS; KANA & KARITJI 1982 Bahasa-bahasa di Irian Jaya: suatu deskripsi singkat, Bahasa dan Sastra).
Wight, Robert L. 1974. Expedition from Kiwi to the area of the Aipki people. Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya Development 3(1): 26-38. Jayapura: Universitas Cenderawasih.
sources.note: No phonology content and no word data at all: the only linguistic remark is that the Aipki 'are distinctive in their dress, their houses.. and probably in their language' and that communication went through one Ngalum-Aipki bilingual; the rest is subsistence, houses, dress, bows, song and dance (musical intervals, not speech).
sources.venue: Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya Development

sources.citation: Dryer, Matthew S. & Sebastian Sauppe (compilers). n.d. Kimki [KIMKI] wordlist. In Wichmann, Soren, Eric W. Holman & Cecil H. Brown (eds.), The ASJP Database. Leipzig: MPI-EVA. asjp.clld.org/languages/KIMKI.
sources.note: wordlist-only data: c. 70 items in ASJP orthography, which does not encode stress; no statement of any kind.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Kimki section c. pp. 467-469.

sources.note: The only published treatment of Kimki by a linguist; snippets show it rests entirely on Rumaropen's wordlist (vocabulary table, pronouns, 4 sentences), so a stress statement is unlikely but the three pages should be checked to close the file.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2017. Language isolates in the New Guinea region. In Lyle Campbell (ed.), Language Isolates, 287-322. London: Routledge. Sec. 3.9 Kimki.

sources.note: Most recent survey entry on Kimki; overview only, but would confirm that no phonological description exists.

sources.citation: Rumaropen, Benny. 2004. Draft Survei Sosiolinguistik pada ragam Bahasa Kimki di Bagian Tenggara Gunung Ji, Papua, Indonesia. Unpublished ms., SIL Indonesia (Jayapura); announced for SIL Electronic Survey Reports but never issued.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only first-hand Kimki data set (c. 250-word phonetic wordlist from Batom and Sabi + 12-15 sentences); its transcriptions carry stress marks, so a stress pattern could at least be read off the list even if the report states no rule. Would have to be requested from SIL Indonesia / SIL Language & Culture Archives.

sources.citation: Whitehouse, Paul. n.d. Type-up of Kimgi wordlist collected by Reimer (and Songkilawang), July 1980, Arbasi village. Unpublished ms. (Usher/Whitehouse collection).

sources.note: Second independent phonetic wordlist of Kimki; if stress-marked it would corroborate or contradict the Rumaropen transcriptions.
